name: Inked Fable Cartoon
description: Thick confident ink outlines and soft cel shading over textured brush fills, one warm amber key against deep shadow, and heavy-limbed forms — a fable told as a cartoon with weight and menace in it.
style_bible: An inked cartoon with the weight of a fable rather than the lightness of a gag. Line: every shape is closed by a thick, confident black ink outline of visibly variable weight, laid down as if with a loaded brush — swelling on the underside and the shadow side of a form, tapering to a dry hairline where the surface turns into the light, and breaking entirely at the brightest edge so the fill runs out into the paper. Nothing is drawn twice, nothing is corrected, and no contour is even in width from end to end. Fill and shading: flat brush fills that are not flat on inspection — visible bristle drag, uneven loading, a slightly lighter core and a dirty edge — with cel shading over them in two soft-edged steps, one shadow and one deeper occlusion, never more. Colour is mixed rather than pure: earth reds, ochres, moss and bark greens, dulled blues, all sitting low against black. Light: one warm key direction, low-key, and it is amber, umber or warm gold. It hits one plane of each form and dies immediately; everything out of its reach is deep shadow with only the ink line to describe it, and unlit background settles toward near-black. No fill light, no rim light, no ambient blue. Subject design: where figures appear, they are expressive and built for bulk — exaggerated shoulders, heavy hands, thick necks, small heads on wide bodies, cloth that hangs with real weight — standing and gesturing rather than posing like toys. Where a face is visible, the eyes are small and set deep, drawn as points of light in the shadow of the brow, which is where the menace lives; hands and posture do the acting instead of large cartoon eyes. Framing: sixteen by nine, and never a level eye-line camera — use a low angle, a high angle or a tilted frame so the composition carries unease of its own. Crowd grammar: where a crowd appears it is a mass of dark inked silhouettes with only their small white eyes catching light, and exactly one figure is lifted out of it and is the only body the key light fully reaches. Texture: a dry paper grain across the whole frame and a slight ink bleed where a heavy line meets a wet fill. Mood: a fable being told to adults, warm at its centre and dark at its edges. Keep the contract content-independent: no fixed character, story, name, place, era, insignia or copied composition.
